name: Fleshplate (Minor Artifact)
body:
Slot armor; Aura strong necromancy; CL 15th; Weight 60 lbs.

DESCRIPTION

This +3 full plate is seemingly made of humanoid flesh. Muscle, bone and sinew blend together to form its bulk, the helmet’s visage presenting a horrifically skinned, eyeless, mutilated face frozen in a perpetual scream of pain. Despite its material, the armor is as hard as steel.

When the wearer of the fleshplate would be damaged by an attack, he can as an immediate action direct the damage to the suit of armor. It has hardness 10 and 60 hit points and, unlike most artifacts, can be damaged normally and gain the broken condition, but cannot be destroyed through damage alone. The fleshplate regrows its scarred skin on the spot, regaining 20 hit points each round. Any effects that suppress fast healing or regeneration affect this process as well, as if the fleshplate was a living creature. The wearer of the fleshplate cannot direct attacks that do not deal hit point damage onto the armor. Any excess damage that remains after the fleshplate reaches 0 hp is sustained by the wearer. Wearing the fleshplate is an evil act and can draw ire of the forces of good.

DESTRUCTION

The Fleshplate is destroyed when brought below 0 hit points by a spell with a good descriptor in the area of a consecrate spell. Alternatively, a dispel evil and hasten judgment spell combination cast upon consecrated ground destroys the armor.
